title: Using Probabilistic Model Rollouts to Boost the Sample Efficiency of Reinforcement Learning for Automated Analog Circuit Sizing
problem: Analog circuit sizing optimization requires extensive circuit simulations, creating prohibitive computational costs and long design cycles. Reinforcement learning methods demand numerous samples to converge on optimal designs.
motivation: Automating analog circuit sizing can dramatically reduce design time and improve solution quality, but simulation costs remain a critical bottleneck limiting practical adoption.
method: The approach combines two reinforcement learning techniques (Model-Based Policy Optimization and Twin Delayed DDPG) into a single algorithm called MBTD3. It trains an ensemble of probabilistic models—multiple predictive models that output probability distributions rather than single predictions—on data from actual circuit simulations. These models then generate synthetic "rollouts" (simulated design explorations) without running the expensive real circuit simulations at each step. For larger circuits, a multi-agent variant simultaneously sizes different circuit sub-blocks (sections of the circuit) using the same shared probabilistic models, reducing the total number of real simulations needed.
key_novelty: The core idea is training multiple predictive models on real simulation data, then using them to generate synthetic simulations, so reinforcement learning can explore circuit designs using far fewer actual circuit simulations.
contributions: Application of Model-Based Policy Optimization to analog circuit sizing problem
MBTD3 algorithm achieving 3x reduction in simulations and 50% reduction in run time versus model-free TD3
Multi-agent MBTD3 variant for hierarchical circuit optimization with 2x simulation reduction
Validation on analog circuits of varying complexity with power/area-optimal solutions

metrics.speedup: 3x fewer simulations (single-agent), 2x fewer simulations (multi-agent), 50% reduction in run time

limitations: Scalability beyond presented test circuits and transferability of learned models to novel circuit topologies not discussed.
primary_theme: Model-based RL for sample-efficient analog circuit design automation
